about: Field Books 1 to 4 of 24: the four found in the slice. Lore only. Each is one ruled page in Plex Mono (lines already broken, at most 58 characters), a sketch for the page's corner, and the single mark it inks on the map. 'loading' is the one line the Loading screen may show.

books.title: LEVEL BOOK 7 · SOUNDING
books.hand: a leveller of the Datum Survey
books.found: under the fallen quadrant's nearest flange, at the foot of the Sounding Ring's rise
page: Run 7. Ring foot to the lagoon post and back.
Out 1,214.6 m. Back 1,214.6 m. Closed to 2 mm.
Good enough for anybody. Not good enough for Hale,
so we ran it again after bread. 1 mm.
The Ring holds level for the whole island now.
It hums when the swell is long. You stop hearing it.
Stores for nine days. Ship due on the 14th.
The tide keepers took their first sluice today
without one of us standing by. Nobody clapped.
It is only a float and a clock.
Mark set at the rise foot. Bronze, flush, arrow up.
If you are reading this you are standing near it.
books.sketch: a levelling staff held upright on a flush bronze stud, the Ring behind it drawn as one tilted ellipse, three tick marks for the swell

inks.what: the approach to the mark at the foot of the Sounding Ring's rise

books.loading: Out 1,214.6 m. Back 1,214.6 m. Closed to 2 mm.

books.title: TALLY OF THE THIRD PAN
books.hand: a Matron of the Pan Houses, two before Ansel
books.found: in the guild house, on the shelf under the bell rope
page: Cut this year by our own house: one pan, the third,
22 paces by 14, dyked in basalt and tarred.
Cost: 40 salt in cord and bronze, 9 weeks, one thumb.
The Gauge walked the new dyke on its second day.
It stood 8 minutes with its ring halfway up the mast.
Then it went back to the sluice. The Reckoner says
that is as near to a welcome as they give.
First lift, 31 baskets. Second, 44.
I have put 5 salt by at the end of the breakwater,
seaward side, under the last capstone,
against the year the pan gives nothing.
It will not come. But I am the Matron and I count.
books.sketch: a plan of the pan grid with the third cell hatched, a small basket tally of five-bar gates down the margin

inks.what: the seaward end of the breakwater

books.loading: It will not come. But I am the Matron and I count.

books.title: A RECKONER'S RULES
books.found: in Brea's house, inside the lid of the cistern box
page: For whoever has the office after me.
1. They do not see you. They see what you stand on.
2. A lit peg-head is a sentence being written.
Do not stand in the middle of it.
3. Wide lamp, walk. Half lamp, stop. Pinhole, be
somewhere else.
4. The Gauge keeps better time than the bell.
Never tell the Matron this.
5. When a line moves, move the pan. It is cheaper
than being right.
6. Rule 5 has worked for 800 years.
I do not know what you do on the day it stops.
I kept a little by on the tallest column of the Shelf.
The climb is the lock.
books.sketch: three lamp irises in a row, wide, half and pinhole, each with one word under it; a stepped column with an arrow at the top

inks.what: the top of the Organ Shelf's tallest column

books.loading: They do not see you. They see what you stand on.

books.title: KITE LINES, SOUTH COAST
books.found: tied to the first line-post on the Organ Shelf rim, in an oiled bag
page: Coast people ask how we cross a ravine with a net.
We do not cross it. The wind does.
Wind from 045, every day it is not dust.
Where it meets a wall of 25 degrees or steeper
it has to go up, and for 40 m it takes you with it.
I have set 5 posts along the Shelf rim.
When the cloth on a post stands straight out,
the lift is on from that post to the next.
When it hangs, walk.
Two cells, cane spars, the bar at your chest.
Never fly in dust. Never fly in a squall.
A Plumb sees a kite at twice the range it sees a goat.
Whistle if you land badly. Somebody will come.
books.sketch: a box kite side-on with its two cells and bridle, a row of five small posts with streamers, an arrow marked 045

inks.what: the first line-post on the Organ Shelf rim

books.loading: We do not cross it. The wind does.
